BiblicalUsage: Ptenon means a bird, a winged creature. It appears once, in Paul's argument about the resurrection body: all flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the bird's flesh is Paul's proof: if God gives each creature its own body, He can give me a new one too.
